Stated Claim / Post Context:
ACT should plug in to balcony-friendly solar revolution: Liberals

Germany has had them for years. Canberra should follow suit, opposition says.

Actual Article Body:
Your digital subscription includes access to content from all our websites in your region.
Access unlimited news content and The Canberra Times app. Premium subscribers also enjoy interactive puzzles and access to the digital version of our print edition - Today's Paper.

More than a million plug-in solar panel systems are powering homes and apartments in Germany, giving renters the benefit of renewable energy and lower power bills.

Login or signup to continue reading

But the technology is banned in the ACT, meaning apartment dwellers are often cut out of the shift to renewable energy , facing high costs of installing rooftop solar and difficult negotiations with neighbours.

The Canberra Liberals want the ACT and federal governments to give Canberra's renters and apartment owners the same access to plug-in solar panels that they say Germany has proved are safe and effective.

Australians should be able to use plug-in solar and batteries from July 1, 2027, and existing rebates should cover the devices, the party said.

Elizabeth Lee, the Liberals' environment and climate change spokesperson, said it was a solar policy that cost taxpayers nothing and would deliver benefits for the growing number of Canberrans living in apartments.

"The Barr government likes to call Canberra a global leader in climate action - so we're calling on the ACT government to match Western Australia by starting its own safety standard consultation, and to make sure rental and unit titles rules don't allow tenants and owners to be unreasonably blocked from installing a system," Ms Lee said.

The Liberals' top ACT Senate candidate, Nick Tyrrell, said Germans could pick the technology up with their local groceries so it should not take years of committee discussions before Australians are allowed to plug in solar panels.

"Almost a third of Canberra homes are rented, and plenty more are apartments without a roof of their own. These are exactly the people who have been locked out of the benefits of solar, and they deserve a better deal," Mr Tyrrell said.

In September, Australia's energy ministers agreed to "explore pathways to support the safe deployment of plug-in consumer energy resource (CER) devices".

"The Commonwealth, in partnership with states and territories, will identify measures that enable the safe use of plug-in CER and report back to Energy Ministers this year on next steps," the communique issued after the ministers' September meeting said.
